VERIDANE - INTERNAL - Product Safety Committee memo PSC-2026-07
Date: 2 Oct 2026     From: Elena Kowalczyk, VP Quality & Product Safety     To: Executive Leadership Team

Subject: GV-400 series combination gas valve - voluntary recall (CPSC Fast Track)

Summary
- Affected units: ~41,200 GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves, date codes 2507-2612, sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters.
- Issue: diaphragm seat can deform under sustained high-inlet-pressure conditions, allowing gas to pass when the valve is commanded closed. 17 field reports of gas odor; 2 reports of delayed ignition causing cabinet damage; no injuries reported.
- Root cause: change of diaphragm compound supplier (Q1 2025); supplier lot material out of spec on compression set. Corrective action complete; replacement valves shipping from Mequon plant since 28 Sep.
- Regulatory: CPSC Fast Track filed 22 Sep; joint recall notice expected the week of 19 Oct. Canada (Health Canada) notification filed.
- Cost: reserve booked in Q3 $21.6M (field replacement, OEM labour reimbursement, logistics). Range $18-26M. Supplier recovery claim of ~$9M lodged, not recognised.
- Customer impact: three OEMs (incl. our 2nd-largest BCV customer) have paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice. Included in updated guidance.

*Quarter ended September 30, 2026 — first draft for release Thursday, November 5, 2026, 4:05 p.m. ET*

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Veridane's growth engine accelerated again in the third quarter. Thermal & Data Center Solutions grew net sales 13.4% year over year, we won two new hyperscale awards, and our data-center cooling backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0% from a year ago. The same quarter also asked us to demonstrate operating discipline, and we responded deliberately on two fronts: we initiated a voluntary recall of our GV-400 series gas valves in coordination with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, and we launched Project Keystone, a cost and productivity program that will deliver $35 million of run-rate savings by the second quarter of fiscal 2027.

Net sales were $412.6 million, down 6.0% year over year, as the decline in our core commercial HVAC and valve business more than offset continued growth in data-center cooling. Adjusted EBITDA was $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin, and adjusted EPS was $0.15. Total backlog stands at $918.0 million, up 13.0% year over year, giving us strong visibility into fiscal 2027.

## Highlights

- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million, including two new hyperscale awards in the quarter.
- Record data-center cooling backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year; total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0%.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million (11.8% margin); adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- GV-400 recall executed on a voluntary, proactive, customer-first basis with the CPSC under its Fast Track program; corrective action complete, replacement valves shipping since September 28, and no injuries reported.
- Project Keystone launched, targeting $35 million of run-rate savings by the second quarter of fiscal 2027.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC).** Net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% from $137.8 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2025. Demand for data-center cooling remains the strongest part of our end markets: we booked two new hyperscale awards during the quarter, and the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger introduced last quarter is now ramping with hyperscale customers. Segment backlog grew to $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year. These systems commission over multi-quarter cycles, so a substantial portion of that backlog converts into revenue in late fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027 — a cadence that is typical of our project pipeline.

**Building Controls & Valves (BCV).** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% from $301.2 million a year ago, reflecting continued softness in commercial construction and a temporary pause in GV-400 orders by some OEM customers ahead of the recall notice. On the GV-400: this was a voluntary, proactive, customer-first action taken with the CPSC under its Fast Track program, covering valves sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters, with parallel notification to Health Canada. We identified the root cause — an out-of-specification diaphragm compound introduced through a supplier lot change in early 2025 — completed corrective action, and have been shipping replacement valves from our Mequon plant since September 28. No injuries have been reported. We recorded a $21.6 million charge in the quarter to cover field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics. With the joint recall notice published and remediation well under way, we expect GV-400 order activity to normalize as affected customers complete their reviews.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year fiscal 2026 guidance to net sales of $1.66–1.70 billion, from $1.78–1.84 billion previously, and to adjusted EBITDA of $205–215 million, from $255–270 million previously. The update reflects continued softness in BCV end markets, the pause in GV-400 orders ahead of the recall notice, and the timing with which our TDC backlog converts into revenue. Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS exclude the GV-400 recall charge recorded in the quarter and Project Keystone restructuring costs of $6.2 million.

Project Keystone is central to our path forward. The program targets $35 million of run-rate savings by the second quarter of fiscal 2027, with the savings building through fiscal 2027 as the actions take hold. Combined with the rising margin contribution of our TDC mix as backlog converts, Keystone underpins our confidence in the earnings recovery ahead. Capital spending remains disciplined and focused on the highest-return opportunities in TDC: $14.9 million in the quarter and $41.8 million year to date.

We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash, and we continue to manage working capital and capital spending with discipline as we fund the TDC growth program.

## Closing

We want to thank our 6,200 employees — especially the quality, engineering and Mequon plant teams who moved quickly on the GV-400 recall — our OEM customers for their partnership through the remediation, and you, our shareholders, for your continued trust. The fundamentals that matter are moving our way: a record data-center backlog, a recall handled quickly and transparently, and a clear cost plan in Project Keystone. We look forward to updating you on our fourth-quarter call.

Sincerely,

Dana Whitcombe
President & Chief Executive Officer

Mark Ostrander
EVP & Chief Financial Officer

# Veridane Fluid Technologies — Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders

*Quarter ended September 30, 2026 — first draft for release Thursday, November 5, 2026, 4:05 p.m. ET*

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Veridane's growth engine accelerated again in the third quarter. Thermal & Data Center Solutions grew net sales 13.4% year over year, we won two new hyperscale awards, and our data-center cooling backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0% from a year ago. The same quarter also asked us to demonstrate operating discipline, and we responded deliberately on two fronts: we initiated a voluntary recall of our GV-400 series gas valves in coordination with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, and we launched Project Keystone, a cost and productivity program that will deliver $35 million of run-rate savings by the second quarter of fiscal 2027.

Net sales were $412.6 million, down 6.0% year over year, as the decline in our core commercial HVAC and valve business more than offset continued growth in data-center cooling. Adjusted EBITDA was $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin, and adjusted EPS was $0.15. Total backlog stands at $918.0 million, up 13.0% year over year, giving us strong visibility into fiscal 2027. Data-center cooling now accounts for over 60% of that backlog, and it is our fastest-growing, highest-visibility book of business.

## Highlights

- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million, including two new hyperscale awards in the quarter.
- Record data-center cooling backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year; total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0%.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million (11.8% margin); adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- GV-400 recall executed on a voluntary, proactive, customer-first basis with the CPSC under its Fast Track program; corrective action complete, replacement valves shipping since September 28, and no injuries reported.
- Project Keystone launched, targeting $35 million of run-rate savings by the second quarter of fiscal 2027.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC).** Net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% from $137.8 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2025. Demand for data-center cooling remains the strongest part of our end markets: we booked two new hyperscale awards during the quarter, and the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger introduced last quarter is now ramping with hyperscale customers. Segment backlog grew to $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year. These systems commission over multi-quarter cycles, so a substantial portion of that backlog converts into revenue in late fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027 — a cadence that is typical of our project pipeline.

**Building Controls & Valves (BCV).** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% from $301.2 million a year ago, reflecting continued softness in commercial construction and a temporary pause in GV-400 orders by some OEM customers ahead of the recall notice. On the GV-400: this was a voluntary, proactive, customer-first action taken with the CPSC under its Fast Track program, covering valves sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters, with parallel notification to Health Canada. We identified the root cause — an out-of-specification diaphragm compound introduced through a supplier lot change in early 2025 — completed corrective action, and have been shipping replacement valves from our Mequon plant since September 28. No injuries have been reported. We recorded a $21.6 million charge in the quarter to cover field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics. With the joint recall notice published and remediation well under way, we expect GV-400 order activity to normalize as affected customers complete their reviews.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year fiscal 2026 guidance to net sales of $1.66–1.70 billion, from $1.78–1.84 billion previously, and to adjusted EBITDA of $205–215 million, from $255–270 million previously. The update reflects continued softness in BCV end markets, the pause in GV-400 orders ahead of the recall notice, and the timing with which our TDC backlog converts into revenue. Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS exclude the GV-400 recall charge recorded in the quarter and Project Keystone restructuring costs of $6.2 million.

Year to date, net sales are $1,261.9 million and adjusted EBITDA is $184.0 million, a 14.6% margin. Project Keystone is central to our path forward. The program targets $35 million of run-rate savings by the second quarter of fiscal 2027, with the savings building through fiscal 2027 as the actions take hold and the actions we have already taken annualizing into the cost base. Combined with the rising margin contribution of our TDC mix as backlog converts, Keystone underpins our confidence in the earnings recovery ahead. Capital spending remains disciplined and focused on the highest-return opportunities in TDC: $14.9 million in the quarter and $41.8 million year to date.

We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash, and we continue to manage working capital and capital spending with discipline as we fund the TDC growth program.

## Closing

We want to thank our 6,200 employees — especially the quality, engineering and Mequon plant teams who moved quickly on the GV-400 recall — our OEM customers for their partnership through the remediation, and you, our shareholders, for your continued trust. The fundamentals that matter are moving our way: a record data-center backlog, a recall handled quickly and transparently, and a clear cost plan in Project Keystone. None of that changes the macro backdrop for our core commercial business overnight, but it does mean the company that meets fiscal 2027 will be leaner, more data-center-weighted and growing where demand is strongest. We look forward to updating you on our fourth-quarter call.

Sincerely,

Dana Whitcombe
President & Chief Executive Officer

Mark Ostrander
EVP & Chief Financial Officer
